ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: There is a particle with a mass of 4 kg moving in the x-y plane. The velocity graph in the x direction and the displacement graph in the y direction are respectively as shown in Figure A and Figure B. According to the graphs, what is the velocity of the particle at time 0?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: At time 0, the velocity of the particle is 5 m/s
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the images: In the attached figure, the left Figure A is the graph of the velocity v in the x direction changing with time t, the vertical axis is labeled v/(m·s^-1), and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s; the graph line corresponds to v=3 m/s at t=0, and reaches 6 m/s at t=2 s. The right Figure B is the graph of the displacement s in the y direction changing with time t, the vertical axis is labeled s/m, and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s; the straight line descends from t=0, s=8 m to t=2 s, s=0 m. Then reason: the velocity component in the x direction at time 0 is vx=3 m/s. The velocity in the y direction is given by the slope of the s-t graph, vy=(0-8)/(2-0)=-4 m/s. Therefore the magnitude of the particle's velocity at time 0 is v=sqrt(vx^2+vy^2)=sqrt(3^2+(-4)^2)=5 m/s.
